structure: Part 1 of 1, the whole ruling file read in full: workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-11-16.md, all 19 lines. Three pieces: the title line "Ruling: Sam, 16 November 2026"; a one-line preamble saying it was given in the overview-and-review build session, answering the status page's question on plants' customs document code; and a numbered list of two decisions. Decision 1 (3 lines) sets plants' customs document code to C085 (CHED-PP), keeps C640 as the animals code (CHED-A), carries the file's only verbatim speech of Sam ("sounds like you've got a good shout on what the plants should be, just do the plants code"), and says it unblocks req-2002 and inc-199. Decision 2 (11 lines) introduces no new "Submitted action required" status, makes a notification submitted with outstanding items SUBMITTED like any other on the ground agreed with Syed Islam on 16 November, names the banner-style alert the dashboard designs under test introduce, withdraws the 9 October afternoon ruling's "Submitted action required" status (req-902's status, req-1987's new status) and the 'Action required' tag on the live-animals list (inc-131's action-required criteria), keeps what submitting records (its date and the outstanding items left at that moment, req-909), lists what comes out with the status until the banner design is agreed (the status tag reads 'Submitted'; the view's action-required warning, its 'Continue' and the review's 'Upload a valid health certificate' error, req-902, req-903, req-907), marks one sentence as the orchestrator's call applying the ruling narrowly (nothing action-required is shown until that design lands), and closes that "Completed" stays out until a real source of completion exists, none does today. Covered: both decisions clause by clause, each withdrawn item, each item that comes out, the orchestrator's call recorded as the orchestrator's not Sam's, the "Completed" line, and four gaps where the file touches something and leaves it open (the banner's own design, wording and placement; when and how anything action-required may be shown once that design lands; what a real source of completion would be; and where the customs document code is shown or captured, since the file names no page, view or field). Decision 1's unblocking of req-2002 and inc-199, and the preamble's framing, are carried in notes as the brief's covers directs. Nothing in this source belongs to another part.

claims.statement: The owner ruled that plants use their own plants-specific customs document code, rather than the animals code.
claims.quote: Sam: "sounds like you've got a good shout on what the plants should be, just do the plants code"
claims.note: New decision. Given in the overview-and-review build session, answering the status page's question on plants' customs document code (the file's preamble). The file records that this decision unblocks req-2002 and inc-199. The file names no earlier report question or conflict id for it.

claims.statement: Plants' customs document code is C085, the CDS document code for the Common Health Entry Document for Plants, Plant Products and Other Objects (CHED-PP). This is inferred rather than verbatim because Sam's quoted words endorse only "the plants code"; the specific value C085 and its CHED-PP expansion are the main session's reading of the ruling, written in the file's own words.
claims.quote: Plants' customs document code is **C085**, the CDS document code for the Common Health Entry Document for Plants, Plant Products and Other Objects (CHED-PP).
claims.note: New decision. The file states C085 in its own words, so the value is not in doubt; the confidence reflects that Sam's quoted speech does not name the code. The file records that this unblocks req-2002 and inc-199.

claims.statement: C640 stays the animals customs document code, for the Common Health Entry Document for Animals (CHED-A).
claims.note: New decision. The file's own words of the decision; Sam's quoted speech covers only the plants half, and his "just do the plants code" leaves the animals code as it is.

claims.statement: The ruling leaves the banner-style alert's own design open: it names the banner as how outstanding actions are shown, and says the dashboard designs under test introduce it, but specifies no wording, no placement and no appearance for it.

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open what a real source of completion would be: it holds "Completed" out until one exists but names no candidate, system or event that would count.

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open where the customs document code is shown or captured: it sets the plants and animals code values but names no page, view, field or data shape that carries them, beyond the preamble's mention of the status page's question.
claims.note: Open point, not a decision. The preamble says the ruling answers the status page's question on plants' customs document code, which is the only hint of where the code appears.
